title: Ransomware data-recovery executive indicted for wire fraud after FBI sting
date_note: Krebs (20 Nov) says the indictment was returned "this week" in Rhode Island; the exact filing date is not stated. 19 Nov is the first publication (404 Media).
summary: Krebs on Security reports that Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar, co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com, was charged with wire fraud in an indictment returned this week in Rhode Island. The indictment alleges the firm routinely paid ransomware groups for decryption keys and charged victims well above what it paid. 404 Media reports prosecutors say the FBI posed as both a ransomware victim and the attacker.
plain: A ransomware recovery company is accused of secretly paying the criminals for decryption keys and charging victims far more. The FBI posed as a victim and as the attacker to catch it.
exec: Recovery firms that allegedly pay ransoms without telling clients can overcharge them; vet any firm before hiring in a crisis.

validation.note: Verify desk read Krebs (20 Nov) and the free lede of 404 Media (19 Nov, paywalled after). Both confirm the name, wire fraud and the FBI sting; Krebs adds routine payments to ransomware groups and Rhode Island. The "three counts", "Kansas business, $720,000" and "$445,000" claims could not be found in readable text and were removed. Each publisher states different facts, so kept single_source.

review.note: Read Krebs (20 Nov) and the 404 Media lede (19 Nov). Date moved from 18 to 19 Nov (404 Media saying Wednesday is not in the readable text; Krebs says only this week). Summary now says the indictment alleges routine payments and higher charges to victims; plain and exec drop unsourced wording; action
